transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... well, I guess I'm here because my eating kind of... went a little off track recently? It sounds a bit silly saying it out loud, but I usually stay really on top of my food tracking. I like to keep things organized, you know? 

But I sort of just stopped caring about it for a while. I was skipping real meals for days and basically just running on coffee and, like, protein bars. I didn't even realize it was happening until I noticed my clothes were hanging really loose on me. I mean, I know I need to do better with taking care of myself, and it's probably not a huge deal, but... does that make sense as a reason to come in? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Did you stop tracking your food and skip meals because you were worried about gaining weight?

Oh, no, no, it wasn't about my weight at all. Um... I mean, I like to stay in decent shape usually, but I definitely wasn't trying to diet or anything. 

I just... I don't know, I just completely lost interest in eating? Like, the thought of actually sitting down and preparing a meal just didn't even cross my mind for a while. I definitely wasn't looking in the mirror worrying about gaining weight or anything like that. I know it sounds a little irresponsible for a guy my age to just forget to eat, so I'm sorry if that's not a very good reason... but I hope that makes sense? Is that a helpful answer?
Did you actually feel hungry during the times you were skipping meals?

Um, honestly... no, not really. That's what was so strange about it. Like I mentioned before with just living on coffee and those protein bars... I just didn't have any physical urge to eat. My stomach wasn't even growling. It's like my appetite just completely shut off. 

I know I already said how my clothes started hanging off me before I even noticed, which I know probably sounds a bit foolish for a guy my age to let happen... I really should have paid better attention to myself. But I genuinely just wasn't hungry at all during those days. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Was there something stressing you or bothering you around the time you lost interest in eating?

Um... well, yeah, I guess there was something. I'm a project management specialist, so I'm usually pretty good at handling stress. But... we had a project sponsor who kind of... questioned my judgment on a few things. It really shouldn't have been a big deal, and I know I should be able to take professional feedback better. 

But... I don't know, it was like the bottom just completely dropped out. I just felt so hollow, and... really ashamed, honestly. I ended up just sitting alone in my apartment, and... well, this is a little embarrassing to admit, but I was actually crying over regular work emails. Emails I normally would have just handled without a second thought. I know that sounds like a huge overreaction for a guy my age, and I'm sorry if it makes me sound like I can't handle my job. But... do you think that could be connected to why I stopped eating? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Did you feel sad or depressed during the time you were skipping meals and feeling hollow?

Um... yeah, I guess you could say that. I mean, I don't want to sound like I was totally falling apart or anything, because I usually keep it together pretty well. But... yeah, after that sponsor questioned my judgment, I just... I felt really, really down. 

Like I was saying, it just felt like the bottom completely dropped out. I just sat there in my apartment feeling so... hollow. And just really ashamed, you know? Like I said, I was crying over just regular work emails, which... I know is really embarrassing to admit. I normally would have just handled them without a second thought. I wasn't trying to be dramatic or anything, I promise. It just felt like this heavy cloud wouldn't lift. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I don't want you to think I'm just feeling sorry for myself.
How long did you feel this heavy cloud and emptiness after the project sponsor questioned your judgment?

Um... well, to be completely honest... it's been going on for a while. I know I really should have just bounced back, being a professional and all, but... it's actually been about three months. 

Ever since that whole crisis with the project sponsor, that... that hollow, ashamed feeling, and just having zero interest in anything... it's just kind of dragged on for the last three months. I really hope that doesn't make me sound weak or incapable. I've been trying my best to push through it and not let it show, I really have. Is... is it normal for a reaction like that to last three months? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Did you lose interest in activities you normally enjoy during those three months?

Um... yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I try to stay active, I really do. Usually, I'm pretty good about keeping up with my hobbies because they keep me grounded, you know? But lately... well, for the past three months, I just haven't had the drive for any of it. 

I usually love hiking and editing photos, and I'm normally really diligent about logging my meals. I even have this woodworking project sitting out in my garage that I was so excited about. But... I haven't wanted to touch any of it. I just haven't had the energy or the interest. I know I should be forcing myself to get out there and do things, and I feel really guilty that I'm just letting it all sit there. I hope it doesn't make me seem lazy... I really am trying to get back to normal. Is it okay that I haven't been doing those things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's been going on.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide during these past three months?

Um... well... I don't want to alarm you, or make you think I'm a danger to myself or anything... because I really would never want to be a burden. But... yeah, things got pretty dark for a little bit. 

I just... I started thinking that everyone at work would probably just be better off if I didn't wake up. Like, it would just solve the problem of me messing things up, you know? And... I feel really awful even admitting this, but right after that awful meeting with the sponsor... I actually said out loud that I should just walk into traffic and be done with it. 

I know that sounds terrible, and I'm so sorry if that's upsetting to hear. I really wasn't trying to be manipulative or seek attention, I promise. It was just a really low moment. I know I shouldn't think like that, and I'm really trying to be more positive. Is it... is it bad that I let myself get to that point? I hope you don't think less of me for it... I'm really trying my best to handle things better.
Did you have any difficulty sleeping during these past three months?

Um... well, sleep has been a little tricky, to be honest. I mean, I really try to get a full eight hours because I know how important rest is for being productive, and I always want to be at my best for the team. But... yeah, it's been hard lately. 

Even when I would go to bed and really try to sleep, I'd just keep waking up at all these weird hours. My brain would just immediately go right back to the deployment plan, obsessing over every little detail of where I went wrong. And then by the time morning rolled around, I just felt completely wrecked instead of rested. 

I'm really sorry if that makes it sound like I don't have good sleep hygiene or something—I really do try to turn off my screens and wind down! It's just that my mind wouldn't let me. Is it normal to have your sleep messed up like that when you're stressed? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need.
Did you find any activities that you normally enjoy to still be pleasurable during the past three months?

Um... no, not really. I know we touched on this a little bit already, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much... I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yeah, even when I tried to force myself to do the things I usually love... it just felt empty. Like I said, I haven't wanted to hike, or edit photos, or even keep up with logging my meals. And that woodworking project in the garage is still just sitting there gathering dust. It's really strange for me, because usually, those are the exact things that keep me grounded and help me recharge. 

I really tried to find some joy in them, I promise I did. I know how important it is to have outlets. It's just... nothing sparked that usual good feeling. I feel bad even saying that, because I know I should be more resilient and find ways to enjoy my downtime. Does that make sense? I hope that answers your question properly... I'm really trying to give you the clearest picture I can.
Have you felt like you've lost interest in things that normally bring you pleasure, or have you still been able to enjoy some activities during the past three months?

Oh... um... well, I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I'm really sorry if I'm making you ask the same things twice. I really want to be helpful and make sure I'm giving you what you need... 

But, yeah, it's pretty much like I was just saying. I really haven't wanted to do any of my usual stuff. The hiking, the photo editing... even just the simple things like logging my meals, which I usually stay so on top of. And that woodworking project in the garage is still just sitting there. I know I should probably just push through and do them anyway, because they usually keep me grounded, but... I just haven't had the interest. 

I hope that's okay to say... I know I shouldn't just let my hobbies go like that. I'm really trying to get back into them, I promise. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you had any periods of feeling somewhat better during the past three months?

Um... well... I want to say yes, because I know I should be bouncing back and handling things better by now. But... if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to be honest with you—it's been pretty consistently bad. 

It really started getting bad after... well, after the project sponsor questioned my judgment on that deployment plan. I know I should have just taken the feedback constructively, like a professional, but... it was like the bottom just completely dropped out. I just sat in my apartment for days, feeling so... hollow. And ashamed. I was actually crying over work emails, which is so embarrassing to admit. I normally would have just handled them without a second thought. 

I'm really sorry, I know that sounds so weak and unprofessional. I'm usually much better at taking criticism, I promise. I just couldn't seem to shake that awful, heavy feeling. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound too incompetent... I just want to make sure you understand how bad it felt.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain over the past three months?

Um... yes, actually. I feel really bad admitting this, because I'm usually so disciplined about my health and my diet. I know how important it is to take care of yourself, especially with a demanding job... I really do. 

But... my eating just went completely off the rails recently. I stopped caring about my food tracking, which I know is terrible. For days at a time, I was just skipping real meals and surviving on coffee and those little protein bars. I know that's not healthy at all, and I should have been making better choices. I didn't even realize how bad it was getting until I noticed my clothes were just... hanging off me. They're all loose now. 

I'm really embarrassed about it. I know I should be managing my weight and my nutrition better than that. I'm trying to get back on track, I promise. Is that the kind of detail you need? I hope I'm not sounding too irresponsible...
Have you felt any pleasure when doing things that you normally find enjoyable, even if you didn't feel like doing them, over the past three months?

Um... well, to be honest... no, not really. I know we sort of touched on this, and I really apologize if I'm repeating myself or not giving you exactly what you're asking for. I just... I want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

But even when I did try to force myself to do things... like, I tried to look at my woodworking project in the garage, just to see if maybe getting my hands busy would help. But it just felt... flat. Like there was no point. And the same with the hiking trails I usually love, or sitting down to edit photos. I just couldn't find any joy in it, even though I know I should. Those things are supposed to keep me grounded, and I really wish I could say they were working for me right now. 

I know it sounds like I'm just not trying hard enough, and I feel awful about that. I really am trying to find the good in things. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too negative... I just want to be honest with you about how it's been feeling.
Have you had any days where you felt somewhat better, or were you consistently feeling down over the past three months?

Um... well, it's pretty much been consistently down. I really hate to admit that, because I know I should be bouncing back by now, and I really have been trying to pull myself out of it. I want to be the kind of person who just shakes things off, you know? 

But ever since that whole thing with the project sponsor... it's just been this constant, heavy, hollow feeling. And the shame, too. It's just... it's really dragged on. It's been about three months now of just feeling like that every single day. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm not putting in enough effort to get better, and I really don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. I am trying. Is it okay that it's lasted this long? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of timeline... I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you felt a lack of pleasure in activities you normally enjoy most of the time over the past three months?

Um... yes, exactly that. I know I sort of just mentioned it, and I really hope I'm not being frustrating by repeating myself... I just want to make sure I'm understanding your questions correctly. 

But yes, ever since that whole project crisis happened, it's just been this... this hollow, ashamed feeling. And that lack of interest in everything... it really has dragged on for about three months now. Almost all of the time during those months, yeah. I really wish I could say I snapped out of it sooner, because I know as a professional I should be more resilient than that. I really am trying to be better about it. 

Did I answer that right? I just want to make sure you have the exact timeline you need for your notes... I hope I'm doing okay with these questions.
Have you had any feelings of worthlessness during these past three months?

Um... worthlessness? I mean... I wouldn't say I felt completely worthless. I know I have value, and I'm generally a capable person. I mean, I have my degree, I have my career... I know I'm not useless. 

I guess I just felt... really disappointed in myself? Like I let everyone down with that sponsor thing, and I should have handled it better. But I don't think I'd use a strong word like worthlessness. I just felt like I wasn't living up to my potential, which is something I really want to work on. I want to be someone people can rely on. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not splitting hairs with the words... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture without sounding like I've completely given up on myself. I really am trying to keep a good perspective on things.
Have you experienced any periods where your depression was so severe that you couldn't get out of bed or take care of your daily needs?

Um... well... I mean, I wouldn't say I was completely bedridden or anything like that. I know how important it is to keep moving, and I really tried to push through it. I didn't want to be a burden on anyone. 

But... I guess things did get a little out of hand at work. I, um... I missed some important handoffs, and I sent out some strategy documents that I guess were... confusing? People couldn't really follow them. And then... well, it's really embarrassing to admit this, and I hope you don't think less of me... but my manager and corporate security actually ended up taking me to the emergency department. I know that sounds terrible, and I should have managed things better before it got to that point. 

And at home... I guess I wasn't doing great either. I sort of stopped cooking proper meals or doing my usual hobbies. Just basic routines kind of slipped away. I'm really sorry, I know I should have been taking better care of myself. I'm trying to get back on track now, I promise. Is it okay that I let things slide that much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest picture, even if it's not very flattering.
Did you experience any period where you felt your depression was so severe that you couldn't take care of your basic needs for at least two weeks?

Um... yes, I think so. I know we sort of just touched on this, and I really hope I'm not being annoying by repeating myself... I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yes, that whole period after the project crisis—that really hollow, ashamed feeling where I just had no interest in anything and couldn't keep up with my routines—that definitely lasted for about three months. It wasn't just a few bad days. It really dragged on for that whole time. I know I should have been able to pull myself together faster than that, especially with my background, and I feel terrible that I let it go on for so long. 

I really am trying to be more proactive now so it doesn't happen again. Did I explain that okay? I just want to make sure you have the right timeframe for your records... I hope I'm being helpful.
